fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says the seven lamps “…are to light the area in front of the lampstand.” Seven little flames, and every one of them points forward. Aaron does exactly that, setting them up facing toward the front, just as the LORD had commanded Moses (Numbers 8:3). I once got called out of a junk drawer for a job, so I know the feeling of being handed a clear assignment and wanting to get it right.

Good try, friend, but moving isn't the first thing the LORD asks. He says, “Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.” Then He spells out how to cleanse them: sprinkle them with the water of purification, have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes (Numbers 8:7). The text does have them brought before the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 8:9), but that comes later. Cleansing is where the LORD starts.

That's right, baker. The text says the Levites came to perform their service at the Tent of Meeting “…in the presence of Aaron and his sons.” Moses is named in that verse too, but as the one the LORD commanded. The Levites serve in the presence of Aaron and his sons, and the elders aren't mentioned there. Think of it like a first day on the job where you're working right next to the people in charge. The verse wraps up by saying they did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses (Numbers 8:22).

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “…at the age of fifty, they must retire from performing the work and no longer serve.” Fifty is the line, and the verse says must. Now hold your hats, because retirement isn't the end of the story. Verse 26 says they “…may assist their brothers in fulfilling their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they themselves are not to do the work.” So they stay around to assist their brothers, but they don't do the work themselves (Numbers 8:26).

problems.problem: The passage says the lamps are to light the area in front of the lampstand, not that their purpose is to light up the work.
Calling washing step one misstates the cleansing instructions: sprinkling with water of purification comes first, followed by shaving and washing clothes.
Moses is named in verse 22. The distinction is that the Levites serve in the presence of Aaron and his sons, not Moses and the elders.
‘No more heavy lifting’ adds a kind of work the passage does not specify and narrows the restriction. It says they are no longer to do the work, though they may assist their brothers.
